title: Review a big Plan one checkpoint at a time
statement: As an architect I can review a large Plan's work one checkpoint at a time, seeing what was done before, what this checkpoint did, and what is to come, so no review is one huge shot
overview:
A Plan of 200 Tasks across 6 phases cannot be reviewed well at the end, in one go. A
checkpoint marks a stretch of the Plan that one review can explain. Reaching it creates a
review of what changed since the previous checkpoint. Passing it lets the next stretch of
work start in a new workspace.

## What is decided

- **Scope.** A checkpoint's review covers what changed since the previous checkpoint. A
  reviewer may reach further back when they choose.
- **Passing does not mean merging.** It means the work can continue in a new workspace.
  Nothing reaches the main branch because a checkpoint passed.
- **Who passes.** Whoever invokes the Plan decides. They may pass every checkpoint
  themselves, or let the agent pass them unless what it found is surprising or urgent.
- **The gate.** Tasks beyond a checkpoint that has not passed are not offered as ready, and
  starting one warns instead of refusing.
- **Size.** A checkpoint is the right size when Change Saga can explain it in five or six
  slides. One that would need ten to twenty should be split.

## Open questions

- **Where a checkpoint lives.** It could be a record on the Plan naming the Tasks that close
  it, with everything they depend on included, or a mark on a phase. Phases say what runs in
  parallel and checkpoints say what is reviewed together, so they may not line up.
- **Judging size before the work exists.** Slides are counted once the review is written. The
  Plan needs an estimate first, perhaps from the stories and Tasks a checkpoint holds.
- **What "surprising" means for an agent.** A departure from the Plan, a Task added or dropped,
  or a blocked note all seem to qualify. The record of a pass should say who passed it and why.
- **How the new workspace starts.** It presumably branches from the passed checkpoint's head.
  How the stretches finally reach the main branch is not decided here.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Reaching a checkpoint creates a review of what changed since the previous checkpoint
A reviewer can widen a checkpoint's review to an earlier checkpoint when they choose
The checkpoint's review shows the Plan's board with work done before, work in this checkpoint, and work to come told apart
The checkpoint's review lists the stories and acceptance criteria its Tasks address
